## The blocking finding was worse than reported — the digest path was broken in BOTH directions

Probing `_check_dockerfile_reference` directly before changing anything:

- `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv@sha256:aaa...` -> REJECTED, with a nonsense message: 'installs uv sha256:aaaa..., but [tool.uv] required-version pins 0.12.7'. The `@` branch of `_image_tag` returned the WHOLE DIGEST as the tag, which then failed the tag-vs-version compare.
- `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7@sha256:aaa...` — tag AND digest, the strongest correct form — ALSO REJECTED, because the `@` branch short-circuits before the tag is read.

So the commit message's 'digest pins stay allowed' was wrong both ways: bare digests were rejected with a confusing message, and the one form that should be ENCOURAGED was rejected too. Only non-uv digests passed, and only by luck of the repository check — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile:19` pins a digest and was passing incidentally.

**Rule chosen:** for uv, the version must be named as the TAG; a digest is accepted only ALONGSIDE it. The reasoning matters — this gate does not exist to make images reproducible (a digest already does that); it exists to prove the image and `[tool.uv] required-version` AGREE. A digest is immutable but OPAQUE: it never states which uv version it holds, so it cannot be read against the pin, and accepting it silently reopens exactly the skew that took production down. For every other image a bare digest remains an exact pin and is still accepted. Code, module docstring, function docstring, failure trailer, commit message and four tests now all state that one rule.

## The vacuous assertions were proven vacuous with a mutant

Disabling detection (`if tag == "latest"` -> `if False`, and the untagged branch likewise), the OLD assertions STILL PASSED — both cases still exited 1 via the unrelated uv-mismatch finding, and the word 'latest' came from the always-emitted trailer. New assertions bind to `path:line: <specific detail>` and fail under the same mutant.

## Both escapes confirmed, not just theorised

- `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM python:latest` matched with `from='--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM'`, which carries no `/:@`, so `_is_registry_reference` skipped it and the image was NEVER INSPECTED. `FROM` now consumes `(?:--\S+\s+)*` as `COPY` already did. A second test guards against 'fail on any flagged line' as a cheap pass.
- ARG templating was INCONSISTENT: `uv:${UV_VERSION}` was skipped entirely while `uv:$UV_VERSION` was rejected — same defect, two behaviours. Now uv templates FAIL (an unprovable pin; `ARG UV_VERSION=latest` is this outage with one extra hop) while non-uv templates are left alone.
- The glob mismatch is fixed by calling the gate's OWN `_dockerfiles()` rather than duplicating its exclusion list, so it cannot drift. This mattered in practice — the worktree has a `.venv` the old glob would have walked.

`from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.acli import AcliClient` — and :99 freezes that
binding into a default expression: `def run_access_check(*, env=None, client_cls=AcliClient, ...)`.

(tests/interfaces/facades/REDACTED_TOKEN.py:210).

ROOT CAUSE FOUND — and re-recorded here because the original write was STRANDED in an agent's
diverged worktree store and never reached the shared tracker. I have independently verified each
of its three load-bearing facts against `origin/main` before recording.

## The mechanism: two independent 4s that are the same 4

    docs/config.md:597                  max_concurrent_gates = 4   ("0 = off (no env override)")
    Makefile:60                         PYTEST_WORKERS ?= 4
    _build-and-test.yml:779-780         "-n is PINNED to the runner's real vCPU count
                                         (ubuntu-latest = 4, macos arm = 3), NOT -n auto"

Four pytest-xdist workers against a four-slot gate-admission semaphore. When more than one worker
lands on a gate-touching test at the same moment, **the suite exhausts its own semaphore** and a
test fails with `GateCongestedError: all 4 concurrent slots busy` — having proven nothing about
the code.

## Reproduced, not inferred

An agent ran the 12 failing tests alone on an otherwise-idle host:

| mode | result |
|---|---|
| serial | **12 passed** |
| `-n 4` run 1 | 3 failed |
| `-n 4` run 2 | 4 failed |
| `-n 4` run 3 | 2 failed |

Passes every serial run, fails every parallel run, and the FAILING SET VARIES between runs — the
signature of a race on a shared resource rather than a defect in any one test. Ten of the twelve
raise `GateCongestedError` by name; two more (`test_cli_retry_*`, and one asserting `11 == 2`)
fail DOWNSTREAM of the same congestion without naming it, which is why a grep for the error
undercounts the blast radius.

## Why this is more than a local annoyance

**The gating CI cell has exactly this shape.** `ubuntu-latest` gives 4 vCPUs, `-n` is pinned to 4,
and `max_concurrent_gates` is 4 with no env override available to widen it per-lane. So this can
produce a **spurious `Verified -1` on any change**, attributing a host-concurrency artefact to the
patchset under test. That is the same class this session has been cataloguing all night — an
infrastructure condition wearing the costume of a verdict — except here it lands on the merge gate.

Note the macOS asymmetry: `macos arm = 3` workers against 4 slots cannot exhaust it, which is part
of why this reads as intermittent rather than deterministic.

## Bearing on the fix

The originally-filed shape (one unit test taking a host-wide slot) is real but too narrow. Thirteen
tests are now known to participate, and the trigger is ordinary parallel execution, not one badly
behaved test. Worth deciding whether:
- `max_concurrent_gates` should exceed the worker count (it has NO env override today, so a lane
  cannot widen it);
- gate-touching tests should be serialised via `xdist_group`, the mechanism `_build-and-test.yml:915`
  already uses elsewhere (`--dist loadgroup`);
- or the tests should not take a real host slot at all.

Whatever is chosen, preserve the refusal's honesty: it currently says, correctly, *"This is HOST
CONGESTION, not a review result — no verdict was produced and nothing about the ticket was
judged."* That distinction is the reason this was diagnosable at all.

THIRD instance tonight, and it reveals a facet the original report missed.

## New fact: the 8,000-char cap is ALSO a completion criterion, not only a plan-review admission limit

Ticket `337e-b558-17a2-49bd`'s close was refused by the COMPLETION VERIFIER, with exactly one
failing criterion, read from its `completion_verifier_fail_v1` sidecar:

    verdict:   FAIL
    findings:  1
    criterion: "ticket description is at most 8,000 characters"

Its description was **8,320** characters. Nothing about the implementation was in question — the
change (Gerrit 2652) was merged, both gates green, all acceptance criteria ticked and evidenced.
The ticket simply could not be closed because its description was 320 characters too long.

So the cap bites in TWO independent places:

1. **`review-plan` admission** — an over-cap description is refused, which is what the original
   report covered.
2. **`verify-completion`** — an over-cap description is a FAILING completion criterion, so the
   ticket cannot close at all.

(2) is the more consequential one and was not in the original report. It means an over-cap ticket
is not merely awkward to revise: it is **unclosable** until someone shortens it, regardless of
whether the work is done.

## Why the composition is worse than either half

Shortening the description is a TEXT change, which invalidates the plan-review attestation
(`stale-material`). So closing an over-cap ticket requires: trim -> re-run `review-plan` (a
15-20 minute billable gate) -> close (a further ~10 minutes). For a ticket whose code merged hours
ago and whose criteria are already met.

## The three instances tonight

| ticket | chars | how it surfaced |
|---|---|---|
| `9183-aaae` (S2) | 7,994 -> 8,088 | correcting a factually wrong AC pushed it over; the re-review the close then demanded would itself have refused admission |
| `bff5-9163` | 11,782 | widening `file_impact` to match the merged commit forced a re-review the description could not be admitted for |
| `337e-b558` | 8,320 | completion verifier FAILED the close on the cap alone |

Each was resolved the same way — relocating evidence prose into ticket comments until the
description fit. That works, and arguably improves the tickets (evidence belongs in comments,
plan belongs in the description). But it is a workaround discovered three times independently,
and the pressure it applies is toward deleting the explanation of a correction at exactly the
moment a correction is being made.

## Additional acceptance criterion this implies

- [ ] The completion verifier's enforcement of the description cap is settled deliberately: either
      an over-cap description should NOT block a close whose criteria are otherwise met (the cap
      exists to bound REVIEW cost, and a close is not a review), or if it should, the refusal must
      name the remedy and the fact that trimming will force a re-review — so the operator learns
      the full cost up front rather than after a 15-minute gate.
